- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.30) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Forecast tends to lag by 1–3 days in downward trends — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for recent negative sentiment.
- After sharp price spikes, model overreacts and forecasts continued rise — reduce forecast by 2–5% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, model often undercorrects — add 0.5–1.0% upward adjustment.
- For 30-day horizon, model overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days) — dampen first 5 days by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–0.30), model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
